newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Italy might lower deficit/GDP targets - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy might lower deficit/GDP targets - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy could lower its deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio target for 1997, bringing it closer to the limits set by the Maastricht Treaty, Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.

"We can set a lower deficit/GDP target for 1997 than the 4.5 percent already set," Ciampi told a press conference on Saturday night after the meeting of the European Union Finance Ministers and Central Bank governors in Ireland.
"Italy will make strong, substantial progress in getting closer to the 3.0 percent target set by the Maastricht Treaty" Ciampi said.
This target is one of the key criteria imposed by Maastricht on countries wishing to sign up for the launch of the single European currency in 1999.

"The real problem is to set a serious and rigorous 1997 budget. That, together with the (convergence) process of Maaastricht and the confidence that it will inspire in markets, are the keys to bringing Italy's public finances back into line," Ciampi told reporters.

Ciampi said he did not want to comment on statements by the European Commission indicating that Italy was among six European countries which, as things stand now, will not qualify for the start of the European single currency.
"During today's meeting the situation of the single European countries was not discussed," he said.

In an official document obtained by Reuters, the commission indicates "signs of economic recovery in a growing number of countries ... except in France and Italy, where such positive signals are still not appearing."
It added that at present seven countries should qualify for entry into the European single currency in 1999, while for six others "a further effort, not beyond reach, is still necessary."
A spokesman for the Commission indicated that Italy was not listed among the first seven countries.

Under Maastricht, founding members of the single currency have to reach the three percent deficit/GDP level in 1997. Latest government targets say Italy's ratio will be 4.52 percent next year and 2.99 percent in 1998. -- Alma Davanzo, Rome newsroom +396 6782501
